follow-up time: Through the entire first year after birth
cohort: 2366 mothers from the 2005-2007 Infant Feeding Practices Study II
finding: Mothers who received labor pain medications were more likely to report delayed onset of lactation, regardless of delivery method.
mod_finding: Compared to vaginal delivery with no pain medication, all modes of delivery with pain medication (vaginal/cesarean, with/without spinal/epidural) were associated with increased odds of delayed onset of lactation.
